text:
Marta (Finance): Heads-up everyone: mid-year budget re-forecast coming Monday. Were instituting a temporary purchase freeze for non-essential spend > $10k starting 2026-07-05 until the reforecast closes. Essential and contractual obligations are exempt — details below. :warning:

Liam (Eng): Clarify non-essential? Are infra refreshes for Dedicated nodes considered essential?

Marta (Finance): Good callout. Essential = SLA or security-related items, renewals already under contract, and pre-approved capital projects. Infra refresh for Dedicated nodes: if tied to SLA or security patching, mark as essential and submit supporting note. If it's discretionary capacity, defer until after reforecast.

procurement-bot: Procurement policy update posted by Marta (Finance): https://redwood.example.com/policies/purchase-freeze-2026 - automated flags will begin July 5.

Ivy (Legal): For multi-year contracts currently in negotiation, keep Legal in loop. Well treat signature deadlines with priority; escalate approvals through Marta if vendor will stop service.

Tori (PM): What about vendor invoices already submitted but not yet paid?

Marta (Finance): Invoices for work already delivered will be processed as usual. The freeze only blocks new purchase commitments and orders > $10k that are not essential.

Amin (Sales): Any changes to the vendor onboarding SLA? We have a partner kickoff next week that needs onboarding cleared.

Marta (Finance): For time-sensitive partner onboarding required for revenue recognition, we will fast-track. Please tag procurement-bot with PRIORITY and include contract reference. Procurement team will triage within 24 hours for priority cases.

Liam (Eng): If a request gets flagged, how will the team know? Will approvers get an alert?

procurement-bot: Flagging behavior: requests > $10k will be auto-flagged during the freeze. Notification sent to requestor, cost center approver, and finance@redwood.example.com. Use the "expedite" checkbox for urgent revenue/SLA tickets.

Tori (PM): Any temporary change to the two-quote rule? We had scoped a $18k integration tool that only has one vendor.

Marta (Finance): The two-quote threshold stays at $20k. Under $20k normal workflow applies. If single-source under $20k, note the rationale in the form and select "single-source". Sourcing will review within the normal SLA.

Ivy (Legal): Quick reminder — if a vendor requires custom indemnities or data processing terms, those are never auto-approved and must go through Legal regardless of amount.

Amin (Sales): Thanks - will tag Legal on the partner deal. Also, is there a contact for emergency exceptions?

Marta (Finance): Escalation contact: finance-ops@redwood.example.com. For exec-level exceptions, CC Raj and I. Well publish an exceptions log after the freeze period for transparency.

procurement-bot: Calendar reminder: Budget re-forecast Q&A session hosted by Finance - Mon 09:30 PT. RSVP link: https://calendar.example.com/event/BRQ-AQ-2026

Liam (Eng): Appreciate the clarity. Please share a simple matrix of what counts as essential vs non-essential.

Marta (Finance): Creating a 1-pager now. Will drop in #all-hands and this channel later today. Thanks for quick questions.

Tori (PM): Noted. Will postpone the non-critical tooling purchase and re-open after reforecast.

Marta (Finance): Thanks everyone. If you have vendor cases that might be impacted, DM me or use procurement-bot with PRIORITY. :lock:
